title: Why contracts were modified, in the departments' own words
question: What reasons do the commission items give for changing a construction contract, and do the reasons differ by department or by builder?
finding: 800 modification items are on file; 359 print a reason that can be sorted and 175 are further phases of Airport design-build contracts. Among the reasons printed: delay, claims and settlements in 58 items ($199.4 million added by those items; most often Tutor Perini Corporation (4)); more capacity on an as-needed or task-order contract in 58 items ($58.1 million added by those items; most often Mik Construction Inc. (2)); conditions found on site in 48 items ($43.7 million added by those items; most often Sierra Mountain Construction Inc (4)); work the owner added or changed in 36 items ($200.1 million added by those items; most often Tutor Perini Corporation (7)); design changes, errors and omissions in 13 items ($14.7 million added by those items; most often Blocka Construction Inc (3)); prices and bids in 7 items ($115.9 million added by those items; most often San Francisco Elevator Services, LLC (1)); final quantities and close-out in 4 items ($655,549 added by those items; most often Arana Group Inc (1)). An item can give more than one reason, and the dollars of an item are counted under each reason it gives. By dollars the largest are work the owner added or changed ($200.1 million) and delay, claims and settlements ($199.4 million). The words kept say what changed, not who was at fault.
how: The commissions that oversee construction (Public Utilities, Airport, Port, Public Works since late 2022, and the transit Board) vote on contract changes above what staff may approve, and on close-outs; those items were read into one record per contract number and department. The first figure is the original amount where an item prints it (or, for the Public Utilities Commission, the award in its minutes); otherwise it is the amount that stood before the first change on file, which already includes earlier staff-approved changes and so understates growth. The latest figure is the final amount at close-out, or the total in the latest item. Where the Board of Supervisors approved the same change as a commission, the commission's row is kept and the Board's dropped; where a numbered modification appears twice, the later row is kept. Design-build and construction-manager contracts, which grow as phases and work packages are added, and professional-services contracts are kept apart from fixed-price construction. The reason is the item's own wording (at most 25 words were kept by the download). It is sorted by the words it uses: conditions found on site (unforeseen, differing site conditions, utilities, hazardous material); work the owner added or changed (additional work, scope, client request); design changes, errors and omissions; delay, claims and settlements; final quantities and close-out; more capacity on an as-needed contract; prices and bids. Builders named beside a reason are those on construction, job-order, design-build and construction-manager contracts, with the number of their items that give it.
limits: The reason kept is the first sentence in the item with causal wording, cut to 25 words, so it may not be the official or the whole reason, and sorting by key words puts some in the wrong group. Staff write these items to justify the change; the builder's account is not in them. An item with no reason kept may give one in a staff report that was not parsed. Dollars are authorizations, and where an item gives two reasons its dollars appear under both.
